newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL COACH CONDEMNS CAMEROON AFTER 2-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL COACH CONDEMNS CAMEROON AFTER 2-0 WIN.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo comdemend Cameroon's rough tactics after his team beat the Africans 2-0 in friendly soccer international on Wednesday.
Cameroon's inexperienced team committed 34 fouls and had midfielder Siewe sent off in the 35th minute of the game, which Brazil won comfortably.
"They came here to stop us playing. We would have scored five if they hadn't stopped every move with fouls," he said. "Cameroon were disappointing."
Barcelona midfielder Giovanni, the only foreign-based player in a makeshift Brazilian side, opened the scoring when he flicked a free kick over a badly-organised Cameroon wall in the 14th minute.

Djalminha, playing his second international, slid in the second in the 48th minute to claim his first goal for his country after an excellent run by Sao Paulo's Denilson, one of three Brazilians making their full international.
Brazil, inspired by the artistry of Palmeiras midfielder Djalminha, created a wealth of chances as they claimed their 12th win in as many full internationals against African opposition.
In the 70th minute, Djalminha nearly scored with as astute chip from 40 metres, goalkeeper Njeukam desperately tipping the ball away just in time.

Brazil striker Oseas, another debutant who plays for local club Atletico Paranaense, twice came close in the first half while Giovanni had a second-half effort cleared off the line after he had dribbled around Njeukam.
The 26,000 crowd watched the second half in almost total silence after their hero Oseas was substituted at halftime.
Cameroon, who beat Togo 4-2 away in their first World Cup qualifier on Sunday and then completed a marathon 26-hour journey to Brazil, were surprisingly short of attacking ideas.
Brazil goalkeeper Zetti had only two saves to make, neither difficult, and some of the Cameroon tackling, on a soaking-wet, barely playable pitch, was frightening.
